Re: Internal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

Member ID: W473677710  
Reference number: POC-CD6AF51965-72160  
Requested service: Rotator cuff repair  
CPT code: 29827  
Date of denial notice: August 10, 2026

Dear Molina Grievance and Appeals Unit:

I appeal Molina’s denial of prior authorization for rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. The clinical record directly addresses that reason for denial.

I have experienced 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not improved with rest. I completed an extensive supervised conservative-treatment program consisting of 24 physical therapy visits over eight weeks, from May 23, 2026, through July 18, 2026. The therapy focused specifically on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, and completion of this treatment is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

In addition:

- I used NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026. It provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- MRI on July 6, 2026, showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- I cannot lift the affected arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- The symptoms remain functionally limiting despite the documented treatment trial.

These records show prolonged symptoms, failure of rest and medication, limited and temporary response to injection, and completion of targeted supervised physical therapy without adequate improvement. They also show a structural full-thickness tear and clinically significant loss of function. Accordingly, the record addresses and satisfies the stated basis for denial concerning conservative treatment.

I request that Molina overturn the denial and authorize the requested rotator cuff repair. Please have the request reviewed by an orthopedic surgeon or other appropriately qualified physician who was not involved in the initial denial.

I also request, without charge, the exact medical-necessity criteria, clinical-review criteria, internal rule, protocol, or similar criterion applied to CPT 29827 in this case, including the applicable version and date; the denial code and its meaning; and the clinical explanation applying those criteria to my medical records. The publicly available Molina material I located does not provide the actual rotator-cuff criteria applied to this case, so I have not quoted the plan’s governing criteria here.

Please include this letter and all submitted clinical records in the appeal file and provide written confirmation of receipt and the appeal determination.

Sincerely,

Rowan Carter
